title: Post-incident: implement autosizing heuristic and noisy-neighbor fingerprint detector
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During the 2026-02-26 dedicated-cluster capacity incident, we observed rapid eviction cascades and latency tail spikes on two customer reservations. Post-incident analysis shows correlated behavior across multiple tenants: sudden sustained token throughput with large prefix variance and KV cache churn. The immediate mitigation (soft-reserve decays + temporary tenant fencing) stabilized nodes, but root causes remain: (1) reservations sized from a single-week usage snapshot that did not account for bursty token arrival patterns; (2) inability to quickly detect and limit stealthy noisy tenants whose per-request patterns mimic normal traffic but cause disproportionate KV cache thrash and GPU memory pressure.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Reservation sizing is currently computed from 95th-percentile sustained throughput; this underestimates short high-intensity bursts that cause eviction storms.
- No explicit fingerprinting to classify noisy tenancy patterns (many short independent requests with large KV regenerations) means we only react post-eviction.
- Burst policy is an all-or-nothing token bucket with fixed decay, which either lets noisy bursts through or clamps well-behaved tenants too aggressively when global pressure occurs.

What we implemented during incident:
- Emergency tenant soft-quarantine on suspected offenders (rollout id: quarantine-2026-02-26).
- Increased reservation decay rate on affected clusters to free headroom.
- Short-term telemetry dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/capacity/2026-02-26-incident (read-only).

Proposed longer-term fixes (this ticket):
1) Fingerprint-based noisy-tenant detector (FNTD) - owner: Marcus Chen
   - Build a lightweight per-tenant feature vector: mean request size, stddev of prefix reuse, KV cache miss-rate delta, inter-arrival distribution, fraction of sub-second responses.
   - Train simple logistic classifier with incidents + synthetic noisy workloads. Output: noisy_score (0..1) updated per-1m.
   - Actionable thresholds: noisy_score > 0.8 => apply graduated throttle; 0.5-0.8 => monitoring + soft-penalty.

2) Reservation autosizing heuristic (RAuto) - owner: Priya Nair (see dependencies for telemetry hooks)
   - Replace single-percentile heuristic with a hybrid metric: sustained_percentile (P95 over 7d) + burst_factor (P99.9 short-window / P95) + eviction_risk (recent node-level eviction rate).
   - RAuto will recommend reservation adjustments and a conservative auto-apply policy for low-risk tenants.

3) Progressive burst governor (PBG) - owner: Marcus Chen
   - Implement a progressive taper instead of flat token-bucket: allow short high-rate bursts but enforce per-tenant tapering that decays faster under node pressure (eviction-aware decay).
   - Provide observability knobs in Console for customers to opt into "burst-friendly" vs "stable-latency" modes.

4) KV cache telemetry & synthetic validators - owner: Carlos Mendes
   - Add per-tenant KV churn metric and an automated synthetic load harness that can replay production-like short-burst workloads in staging clusters to validate RAuto and PBG.

Acceptance criteria:
- FNTD deployed to canary clusters and false positive rate <= 5% on labeled dataset; noisy detection reduces median node eviction rate by >= 60% during injected noisy workload tests.
- RAuto recommendations generated for 100% of reservations in test cluster and when auto-applied in safe-mode causes <= 3% impact on unaffected tenants.
- PBG rollout demonstrates 30-50% reduction in 99.9th latency percentile during controlled burst tests without reducing throughput for normal traffic.
- Dashboard telemetry surfaces noisy_score, reservation_recommendation, and burst_state per-tenant.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (canary): Deploy FNTD read-only + RAuto recommendation engine to canary clusters (runtime-1.23-canary). Gather signals for 72h.
- Week 2 (pilot): Enable graduated throttles + PBG in two low-risk clusters behind feature flag. Run synthetic validator daily.
- Week 3 (gradual production): Expand to additional clusters, expose Console controls to customers, and tighten thresholds based on telemetry.

Risks & mitigations:
- False positives throttling paying customers: start with read-only and advisory mode; auto-apply only for tenants flagged as high eviction risk and with no active customer traffic SLA (low-tier).
- Classifier model drift: retrain weekly with new incidents + synthetic data; add human-in-the-loop review for new high-confidence detections.
- Complexity in upgrade path for Private deployments: provide opt-out flags and documentation for ops teams.

- Initial PR for soft-quarantine: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1426
- Telemetry dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/capacity/2026-02-26-incident

Next steps (owners & ETA):
- FNTD prototype (Marcus) by 2026-03-07 -> deploy read-only (ETA met).
- RAuto draft algorithm (Priya) by 2026-03-10 -> collect recommendation logs (in progress).
- PBG prototype (Marcus + infra) by 2026-03-14 -> feature-flagged pilot scheduled.
- Synthetic harness (Carlos) by 2026-03-18 -> end-to-end validation run.
